note: The .lzma (LZMA alone) format over lzma1 0.6.1 (a port of XZ for Java), where CyberChef uses lzma-js. Compression Mode is the level parameter with the same 1 to 9 range and CyberChef's default of 7; there is no level 0, because the format has no store mode. The 13-byte header and the output are the same format, so xz --format=lzma, 7-Zip and Python's lzma module read the output, but the bytes differ from CyberChef's (a different encoder), and the outputs are pinned to lzma1 0.6.1. Out-of-range levels are E_RANGE. Cross-checked (40 inputs of 0 to 128 KiB, modes 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 against levels 1, 2, 4, 6, 7 and 9): CyberChef decompresses everything written here and this decompresses everything CyberChef writes. CyberChef's default is mode 7, the same as here.

The .lzma format, with no options, as CyberChef's operation has none. Output is the same bytes CyberChef gives for a valid stream. The header is checked (a short header or a properties byte out of range is E_COERCE), and a declared size above the value limit is E_LIMIT_VALUE before anything is decoded. An unknown size (all 0xFF) is decoded only up to the limit: more output is E_LIMIT_VALUE, the decompression bomb rule of the wave 6 conventions. Truncated, corrupt data, and output whose length differs from the declared size, are E_COERCE. Cross-checked, see LZMA Compress. One CyberChef defect: its decompressor returns a JavaScript string for text and converts it back with Latin-1, so UTF-8 text whose characters are all at most U+00FF (an accented Latin text) comes back with each accent as a single byte, not as the UTF-8 sequence; this op returns the exact bytes.
